executive_summary: Product Vision: Develop a greenfield real-time multiplayer typing race MVP enabling 2–8 players to compete in private rooms via shareable links. Current State: Repository initialized with basic scaffold (Docker Compose, TS configs) but lacks business logic; no CI/CD or production infrastructure active. Scope: Private room creation, real-time WebSocket synchronization, server-authoritative game state validation, and persistent results storage. Excludes public matchmaking, social features, and mobile optimization for this phase. Assumptions: Managed PostgreSQL and Redis instances available; deployment targets standard cloud PaaS with sticky session support for WebSocket affinity. Development environment mirrors production stack via Docker Compose. Problem Framing: Users need frictionless competition without complex setup or social overhead; current solutions lack real-time fairness. Goals: Achieve <100ms round-trip latency for game state updates, ensure 99.9% uptime for room sessions, prevent cheating via server-side keystroke validation. Deliver functional MVP within sprint cycle. Non-Goals: Public leaderboards, user profiles beyond basic auth, mobile responsiveness, voice chat. Success Metrics: <100ms latency on 95th percentile, 0% cheating incidents in test suite, 100% room creation success rate under load.
architecture_notes: Backend Core: Node.js/Express REST API handles authentication (JWT/HTTP-only cookies), room lifecycle, and passage data. Dedicated Socket.io server manages real-time race loop. Game Engine is pure JavaScript state machine per room (CREATED → JOINED → READY → RACING → FINISHED) stored in Redis for hot access and crash recovery. Real-Time Sync: Client keystrokes validated server-side against passage text to prevent cheating. Position updates broadcast at 100ms intervals via Redis Pub/Sub to support horizontal scaling. Clients use interpolation to smooth visual movement between server ticks. Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript. Uses HTML5 Canvas for 60fps race track rendering. State management splits between React Context (global game state) and local component state. Socket.io-client handles WS connections with exponential backoff reconnection logic. Data Layer: PostgreSQL stores persistent entities (Users, Rooms, Games, Passages, GameSessions). Redis stores ephemeral room state, player progress, and acts as Pub/Sub broker. Indexes on room_id, user_id, and game_id ensure query performance. Security & Scaling: JWT auth with short expiry (15m). Sticky sessions required at load balancer level for WS affinity. Redis Pub/Sub enables cross-instance broadcasting. Input sanitization on all text fields to prevent XSS. Boundaries: Server owns game logic and state; Client owns rendering and input capture. No client-side trust for game state. Integrations: Prisma ORM for DB, Redis Client for Pub/Sub, Socket.io for WS. Docker Compose for local dev environment. Risks & Tradeoffs: WebSocket affinity is single point of failure if sticky sessions fail; mitigation involves robust reconnection logic and state recovery from Redis. Server-side validation adds latency; mitigation involves optimizing validation logic and using efficient string comparison algorithms.
